Human operators will remain important for safety-critical oversight, regulatory compliance, emergency judgment, and physical plant coordination, especially in nuclear and complex grid operations, but many routine monitoring and control tasks can be automated or centralized. Demand elasticity is low because cheaper operator labor does not cause society to consume proportionally more grid operations; electricity demand may grow, but staffing is constrained more by infrastructure, regulation, and reliability requirements than by operator cost. Because disruption is high and demand expansion is unlikely to absorb productivity gains, the net effect is replace.

title: Preschool and childcare center directors
rationale: AI can materially assist the office and knowledge-work portions of this job, including budgeting, scheduling, compliance documentation, parent communications, curriculum planning, staff training materials, and recordkeeping. However, the core role still depends on onsite leadership, trust with parents, supervision of staff, handling unpredictable child and facility issues, and accountability under licensing and safety regulations. Demand elasticity is low because the number of centers and directors is constrained by birth rates, childcare affordability, staffing ratios, facilities, and regulation rather than by director productivity alone. Because disruption remains moderate rather than high, AI is more likely to augment administrative efficiency than fundamentally replace the occupation.

title: Preschool teachers
rationale: AI can help preschool teachers with lesson planning, activity ideas, developmental documentation, parent communication, translation, and individualized learning materials. However, the core job is hands-on supervision, emotional support, classroom management, safety, play facilitation, and relationship-building with very young children, all of which require physical presence and are constrained by licensing and child-to-teacher ratios. Demand is moderately elastic because childcare and early education are expensive and many families would use more or better services if costs fell, but demand is capped by demographics, facilities, regulation, and parents' preference for human caregivers. Because disruption is low-to-moderate rather than high, the occupation is best classified as resilient.

title: Private detectives and investigators
rationale: AI can substantially improve the digital and cognitive parts of this job, including public-record searches, social-media and OSINT analysis, skip tracing, fraud-pattern detection, video review, and report drafting. However, a large share of the occupation still depends on legally compliant field surveillance, interviewing, judgment under uncertainty, and gathering admissible evidence in real-world settings, which keeps disruption below the high-disruption threshold. Demand could expand moderately if investigations and background checks become cheaper, especially for small businesses, insurers, attorneys, and individuals, but legal, privacy, and case-specific constraints limit runaway growth. Because disruption is meaningful but not enough to reshape the entire occupation, the net effect is resilient rather than replace or restructure.

title: Probation officers and correctional treatment specialists
rationale: AI can materially affect the paperwork-heavy and cognitive parts of this occupation, including drafting case reports, maintaining files, risk scoring, scheduling, monitoring alerts, and matching clients to services. However, the core work still depends heavily on human interviews, counseling, field visits, court testimony, safety judgment, and legal accountability in unpredictable real-world settings. Demand could expand moderately if AI lowers caseload burden, because agencies may supervise more people in the community or provide more intensive rehabilitation, but employment is constrained by courts, offender populations, public funding, and statutory requirements. Because disruption is meaningful but not high enough to displace the core human role, the occupation is best categorized as resilient.

title: Producers and directors
rationale: AI will materially change producers’ and directors’ workflows through script analysis, budgeting and scheduling tools, casting support, previsualization, virtual production, generative video, editing, music, effects, and marketing optimization. However, the core job still depends heavily on human taste, leadership, relationships, financing, on-set coordination, actor direction, negotiation, and accountability for the final creative product. Demand elasticity is high because cheaper production can unlock many more films, shows, advertisements, branded videos, social media productions, and niche streaming projects, even though audience attention and funding constraints limit infinite expansion. Because disruption is high but cheaper output is likely to generate substantially more productions, the occupation is best categorized as augment rather than replace.

title: Project management specialists
rationale: Project management is predominantly cognitive, digital, and communication-heavy: planning schedules and budgets, producing documents, tracking milestones, summarizing meetings, identifying risks, and coordinating workflows are all areas where AI tools can materially improve productivity. However, the occupation also depends heavily on stakeholder trust, negotiation, accountability, conflict resolution, and domain-specific judgment, which limits full automation. Demand elasticity is moderate because cheaper project coordination could let organizations run more projects and give smaller teams access to formal project management, especially in IT and business operations, but the number of projects is still constrained by capital budgets, staffing, and strategic priorities. The result is restructuring: fewer workers may be needed for routine reporting and coordination, while successful project managers will shift toward higher-level judgment, stakeholder management, and AI-enabled portfolio oversight.

title: Property appraisers and assessors
rationale: A large share of appraisal and assessment work is data-driven: verifying records, analyzing comparable sales, applying valuation models, maintaining databases, and writing standardized reports, all of which are directly affected by automated valuation models, GIS data, computer vision, and generative AI. Human site visits, local judgment, licensing requirements, and the need to defend valuations in disputes limit full automation, especially for complex commercial or unusual properties, but routine residential and mass assessment work are highly exposed. Demand is relatively inelastic because appraisals are mostly triggered by real estate transactions, lending, taxation, insurance, or legal requirements rather than by discretionary consumption. Cheaper appraisals may enable more frequent monitoring, but not enough to offset major productivity gains in standardized valuation work, so the occupation is likely to see replacement pressure.

title: Property, real estate, and community association managers
rationale: AI and property-management software can substantially automate the digital and administrative parts of the job, including rent collection, vacancy listings, tenant communications, maintenance-ticket triage, lease explanations, budgeting, and routine compliance documentation. However, the core role still involves on-site inspection, contractor coordination, emergency response, showing properties, board and tenant relations, and resolving ambiguous interpersonal disputes, so AI changes the workflow more than it fully substitutes for the manager. Demand is fairly constrained by the number of managed properties, housing units, HOAs, and commercial sites, though cheaper service may bring some small landlords or associations into professional management. Because disruption is meaningful but not above the high-disruption threshold, the occupation is best classified as resilient rather than replace or restructure.

title: Psychiatric technicians and aides
rationale: Most core tasks for psychiatric technicians and aides require in-person care: observing patients in real settings, helping with bathing/eating, escorting patients, administering medications under supervision, de-escalating conflict, and sometimes physically restraining patients. AI can improve documentation, handoff notes, risk alerts, remote monitoring, and therapeutic activity planning, but it cannot replace the continuous human presence and physical judgment needed in psychiatric and residential facilities. Demand elasticity is moderate because mental health and substance-use care have substantial unmet need, but expansion is limited by reimbursement, facility capacity, licensing, safety rules, and required staffing ratios. Because disruption remains low-to-moderate even though AI may augment workflows, the occupation is best classified as resilient.

title: Psychologists
rationale: Psychologists perform highly cognitive and language-intensive work, including interviewing, assessment, diagnosis, treatment planning, counseling, research, and report writing, many of which AI can assist through documentation, screening, test interpretation, CBT-style tools, and decision support. However, the core therapeutic relationship, crisis judgment, licensure, confidentiality, school/legal accountability, and complex human observation limit full automation, so disruption is high but not maximal. Demand elasticity is high because mental health, school assessment, behavioral intervention, and organizational psychology services are heavily constrained by cost, provider shortages, and access barriers. Because cheaper AI-enabled workflows would likely expand the amount of psychological support delivered rather than simply reduce headcount, the occupation is best categorized as augment.

title: Public relations and fundraising managers
rationale: This occupation is heavily language- and strategy-based: drafting releases and speeches, monitoring media and social trends, segmenting audiences, preparing grant materials, and personalizing donor outreach are all directly affected by generative AI and analytics tools. However, the core managerial work still depends on judgment, reputation risk management, executive advising, staff leadership, media relationships, and face-to-face donor cultivation, which limits full automation. Demand could expand as cheaper communications and prospecting let organizations run more targeted PR and fundraising campaigns, especially smaller nonprofits, but attention, donor capacity, trust, and organizational budgets constrain unlimited growth. Because disruption is high but demand elasticity is only moderate, the occupation is likely to be restructured rather than replaced or broadly expanded.

title: Public relations specialists
rationale: Public relations work is heavily language-based and digital: drafting press releases, speeches, social posts, media pitches, sentiment summaries, and response plans are all areas where AI tools are already materially useful. Human judgment, relationship management with journalists and stakeholders, crisis sensitivity, and public-facing accountability still matter, but many routine writing and monitoring tasks will be transformed. Demand could expand as smaller organizations, nonprofits, executives, and individuals can afford more sophisticated communications support, but media attention and reputation management are partly zero-sum and constrained by trust and relationships. Because disruption is high while demand expansion is meaningful but not enough to fully absorb productivity gains, the occupation is best classified as restructure.

title: Public safety telecommunicators
rationale: Public safety telecommunicators perform largely language-based, digital, protocol-driven work: receiving calls or texts, extracting facts, classifying incidents, entering records, routing resources, and giving scripted instructions. AI speech recognition, translation, call summarization, location inference, triage decision support, and automated dispatch recommendations can materially change the core workflow, though high-stakes judgment, empathy, liability, and human oversight will keep people in the loop. Demand is highly inelastic because the number of emergencies and required public-safety responses is driven by population and incidents, not by the price of dispatch labor. Since disruption is high and cheaper service would not generate much additional call volume, productivity gains are likely to reduce staffing needs over time, even if full automation is constrained.

title: Purchasing managers, buyers, and purchasing agents
rationale: Purchasing work is heavily cognitive and digital: supplier comparison, price analysis, RFP and contract drafting, inventory records, spend analytics, and compliance monitoring are all in AI's direct path. However, the occupation also depends on human negotiation, vendor relationships, product judgment, site visits, accountability, and resolving supplier problems, which keeps disruption below the very highest levels. Demand is moderately elastic because cheaper procurement tools could let organizations analyze more suppliers, manage tail spend, monitor risks, and professionalize purchasing, but the total volume of goods and services bought is still constrained by business operations. The result is restructuring: routine purchasing-agent tasks are likely to be automated, while remaining workers focus more on strategic sourcing, supplier risk, negotiation, and oversight of AI-enabled procurement systems.

title: Quality control inspectors
rationale: Quality control inspection is partly in AI's path because computer vision, sensors, 3D scanning, anomaly detection, and automated reporting can take over many routine visual and measurement tasks, especially in high-volume manufacturing. However, the occupation still involves physical presence, handling materials, using gauges and test equipment, interpreting production context, and troubleshooting process problems, so AI is more likely to reshape workflows than fully absorb the role across all settings. Demand for inspection is only moderately elastic: cheaper inspection may lead firms to inspect more items and collect more quality data, but total demand is constrained by manufacturing output, compliance requirements, and the fixed need to ensure product quality. Because disruption is substantial but not above the high-disruption threshold, the occupation fits the resilient category.

title: Radiation therapists
rationale: Radiation therapists use sophisticated digital equipment and documentation systems, and AI can improve tumor localization, patient setup verification, quality checks, scheduling, and recordkeeping. However, the core job still requires licensed in-person patient positioning, safety protocol execution, monitoring, communication, and coordination with the oncology team, making full automation difficult over the next decade. Demand is relatively inelastic because radiation therapy is driven mainly by cancer incidence and clinical guidelines; cheaper or faster delivery may improve access somewhat but will not cause patients to consume many times more treatments. Because disruption is moderate rather than high, the occupation fits the resilient category despite some workflow changes and efficiency pressure.

title: Radiologic and MRI technologists
rationale: AI can materially assist parts of the job such as protocol selection, image quality checks, dose optimization, scheduling, documentation, and flagging whether additional images may be needed. However, the core work still requires in-person patient preparation, positioning, safety screening, contrast administration, equipment operation, and handling patients who may be injured, anxious, or immobile. Demand for imaging is relatively inelastic because scans are driven by medical need, physician orders, reimbursement rules, and scanner capacity, so cheaper technologist labor would not create dramatically more imaging volume. Because disruption is moderate rather than high, the occupation is best categorized as resilient even though AI will change workflows at the margins.

title: Railroad workers
rationale: AI and automation can materially affect train operation, yard scheduling, dispatch coordination, signal monitoring, predictive maintenance, ticketing, and some inspection tasks, and railroads already use automated and remote-control systems in some settings. However, much of the work still involves safety-critical real-world presence, route familiarity, equipment handling, passenger interaction, outdoor yard work, and federally regulated human accountability, which limits full substitution over the next decade. Demand elasticity is low because rail freight and passenger volumes are constrained by infrastructure, routes, shipper needs, regulation, and overall transportation demand rather than the labor cost of railroad workers alone. Because disruption is meaningful but not high enough to fully reshape the occupation’s hands-on and safety-critical core, the net effect is resilient.

title: Real estate brokers and sales agents
rationale: AI can materially affect many core broker and agent tasks: pricing comparisons, listing descriptions, advertising, lead qualification, property search, document preparation, transaction tracking, and client communications. Human trust, negotiation, local knowledge, licensing, and in-person showings still matter, but a large share of the workflow is information-heavy sales and coordination that can be automated or unbundled by AI-enabled platforms. Demand elasticity is low because the number of home purchases, relocations, and commercial property transactions is constrained by housing supply, financing conditions, demographics, and business formation rather than by agent labor cost alone. Because disruption is high while cheaper brokerage services are unlikely to create proportionally more transactions, AI is more likely to reduce required headcount and commissions than expand employment.

title: Receptionists
rationale: Receptionists perform many routine language and coordination tasks—answering calls, routing inquiries, scheduling appointments, entering information, and handling correspondence—that AI voice agents, chatbots, scheduling systems, and self-service kiosks can increasingly perform. Some duties still require physical presence, interpersonal judgment, visitor management, and security-related handling, which prevents the disruption score from being even higher. Demand elasticity is low because organizations generally do not need dramatically more front-desk interactions if they become cheaper; they are more likely to consolidate coverage or substitute automated systems. Because disruption is high and expanded demand is unlikely to offset productivity gains, the occupation fits the replace category.

title: Recreation workers
rationale: Recreation workers’ core tasks are in-person, social, and safety-oriented: leading groups, adapting activities, motivating participants, supervising youth or older adults, and responding to injuries. AI can help with peripheral tasks such as generating activity plans, newsletters, schedules, promotional materials, forms, and modifications for different participant needs, but it does not replace the real-world presence and interpersonal leadership central to the job. Demand could expand moderately if program design and administration became cheaper, especially in senior care, community centers, and youth programs, but growth is constrained by facilities, staffing ratios, budgets, and the need for human supervision. Because disruption is low-to-moderate, the occupation is best classified as resilient.

title: Recreational therapists
rationale: Recreational therapy includes some cognitive and administrative work—assessment, treatment-plan design, documentation, and progress analysis—that AI can help streamline. However, the core job is hands-on, interpersonal, and safety-sensitive: motivating patients, leading activities, adapting in real time, assisting people with disabilities, and working in clinical or community settings. Demand could expand moderately if services became cheaper, especially for aging populations, mental health treatment, addiction recovery, and underserved care settings, but reimbursement, staffing models, and the need for in-person engagement limit explosive growth. Because AI is more likely to support planning and documentation than replace the embodied therapeutic role, the occupation is best classified as resilient.

title: Registered nurses
rationale: AI will materially affect parts of registered nursing such as documentation, care-plan drafting, patient education, triage support, remote monitoring, and decision support. However, the core of the job still requires licensed in-person clinical judgment, medication administration, patient assessment, coordination with care teams, emotional support, and physical handling in unpredictable healthcare settings. Demand elasticity is moderate because aging, chronic disease, home health, and underserved care create latent demand, but utilization is constrained by reimbursement, staffing models, regulation, and the need for hands-on care. Because disruption remains moderate rather than high, the occupation is best categorized as resilient.

title: Rehabilitation counselors
rationale: AI can materially assist rehabilitation counselors with intake summaries, documentation, benefits and resource navigation, vocational matching, progress tracking, and drafting rehabilitation plans. However, the core work depends on trust-based counseling, empathy, clinical judgment, advocacy, coordination with families and agencies, and adapting to clients’ disabilities and real-world constraints, so AI is more likely to support than replace the central relationship. Demand has some elasticity because disability, aging, veteran, and employment-support needs are substantial and often underserved, but public funding limits, licensing rules, and the need for human care constrain expansion. Because disruption is meaningful but not high enough to reshape the occupation’s core, the net effect is resilient.

title: Respiratory therapists
rationale: Respiratory therapy includes some cognitive and data-oriented tasks—interpreting pulmonary tests, monitoring ventilator settings, documenting progress, and educating patients—that AI decision support, remote monitoring, and automated charting can improve. However, the core work is still bedside and hands-on: assessing patients, managing equipment, responding in emergencies, performing airway clearance, and coordinating care in unpredictable clinical settings. Demand is moderately elastic because cheaper monitoring and workflow support could expand home care, outpatient management, and chronic respiratory disease services, but total need is still constrained by disease prevalence, staffing regulations, and clinical supervision requirements. Because disruption remains moderate rather than high, the occupation is best categorized as resilient.

title: Retail sales workers
rationale: Retail sales work is partly in AI's path because product recommendations, basic customer questions, checkout, inventory lookup, promotions, and online sales support can be handled by chatbots, kiosks, self-checkout, and recommendation systems. However, much of the occupation still requires in-person presence, interpersonal persuasion, handling merchandise, stocking, monitoring the store environment, and assisting customers in unpredictable physical settings. Demand elasticity is low because cheaper sales assistance does not make consumers buy vastly more retail goods; spending is constrained by income, store traffic, and the shift toward e-commerce. The occupation is therefore best classified as resilient because AI will change many tools and workflows, but the core in-store service role is not fully automatable over the next decade.

title: Roofers
rationale: Roofing is overwhelmingly physical, on-site work involving climbing, lifting, removing materials, cutting, fastening, sealing, and handling varied roof conditions in unsafe and unpredictable environments. AI can help at the margins with drone inspections, measurement, estimating, scheduling, and customer quoting, but it does not materially automate the core installation and repair tasks over the next decade. Demand is relatively inelastic because roofs are replaced or repaired based on building stock, weather damage, age, and construction activity, though lower costs could modestly increase preventive maintenance or upgrades such as solar or green roofing. Because disruption to the core work is very low, the occupation is best categorized as resilient.

title: Sales engineers
rationale: Sales engineers do a large amount of cognitive, language-based work that AI can materially assist: preparing technical presentations, drafting proposals, answering product questions, configuring solutions, summarizing customer requirements, and supporting troubleshooting. However, the role also depends heavily on trust-building, persuasion, negotiation, account strategy, and understanding messy customer environments, so AI is more likely to change workflows than fully remove the human role. Demand elasticity is moderate because cheaper technical sales support could let firms cover more accounts, customize more solutions, and sell to smaller customers, but customer buying cycles, budgets, and relationship constraints limit expansion. Because disruption is high but demand expansion is only moderate, the occupation is best categorized as restructure.

title: Sales managers
rationale: Sales managers do substantial digital and cognitive work—CRM analysis, forecasting, territory planning, performance monitoring, customer segmentation, training design, and written communication—that AI can already accelerate significantly. However, the occupation also depends on leadership, motivation, hiring judgment, conflict resolution, customer relationship management, and accountability for revenue outcomes, which limits full automation. Demand is moderately elastic because cheaper sales analytics and coaching could help firms pursue more segments, channels, and customers, but managerial headcount is still constrained by organizational structure and spans of control. The result is restructuring: AI will change the skill mix and allow each manager to oversee more data-driven selling activity, but it is unlikely to eliminate the role broadly.

title: School and career counselors and advisors
rationale: AI can materially change many core tasks: interpreting assessments and student data, generating academic or career plans, answering college and financial-aid questions, helping with résumés and applications, and maintaining records. However, the occupation also depends heavily on trust, empathy, mandated reporting, crisis judgment, family and teacher coordination, and school-based presence, which limits full automation. Demand is moderately elastic because many students and workers are underserved and could use more personalized guidance if it were cheaper, but public school staffing, credentialing, budgets, and institutional ratios cap how much headcount expands. Because disruption is high but demand expansion is not strong enough to fully absorb productivity gains, the occupation is likely to be restructured around AI-enabled triage, advising tools, analytics, and higher-touch human counseling.

title: Secretaries and administrative assistants
rationale: Most core tasks for secretaries and administrative assistants are digital, routine, and language- or coordination-based: scheduling, drafting emails and memos, preparing documents, maintaining records, routing messages, and basic bookkeeping. AI assistants, workflow automation, transcription, document generation, and calendar tools already substitute for substantial portions of this work, though some roles still require interpersonal judgment, office presence, and domain-specific knowledge in medical, legal, or executive settings. Demand elasticity is low because organizations need administrative support roughly in proportion to their scale, managers, patients, or offices; making the work faster does not create a need for dramatically more scheduling or filing. Because disruption is high and demand expansion is limited, productivity gains are likely to reduce headcount or allow each assistant to support more people, fitting the replace category.

title: Securities, commodities, and financial services sales agents
rationale: The occupation is highly exposed because much of the work is digital and cognitive: market monitoring, securities analysis, valuation, pitch materials, prospecting, client communications, and trade execution are all areas where AI and automation are already useful or mature. However, relationship-building, trust, regulatory accountability, negotiation, and high-stakes client judgment remain important human components, especially in wealth management and investment banking. Demand elasticity is moderate: cheaper advice and analysis can expand access for smaller investors and firms, but the number of major deals, trades needing human intermediation, and regulated client relationships is not unlimited. The result is restructuring rather than outright replacement: fewer workers will be needed for routine trading, research, and document production, while successful agents will use AI to cover more clients, personalize advice, and focus on complex sales and relationship management.

title: Security guards and gambling surveillance officers
rationale: AI will materially affect surveillance-heavy portions of the job through video analytics, anomaly detection, automated access control, alarm triage, and report drafting. However, the core work for most security guards still requires physical presence, deterrence, patrols, responding to incidents, interacting with the public, and de-escalating unpredictable situations. Demand is relatively inelastic because businesses, casinos, schools, hospitals, and events need a certain level of security coverage, but cheaper monitoring is more likely to reduce staffing ratios than create much more guard employment. Because disruption is moderate rather than high, the occupation fits the resilient category despite pressure on some surveillance-focused roles.

title: Semiconductor processing technicians
rationale: AI will materially affect semiconductor processing through automated defect inspection, anomaly detection, predictive maintenance, process optimization, and decision support for setting equipment parameters. However, the occupation still requires cleanroom presence, equipment loading and monitoring, physical troubleshooting, precise handling, and coordination with engineers, so AI changes many workflows but does not fully absorb the core job. Demand elasticity is relatively high because semiconductor demand is expanding across AI, vehicles, medical devices, industrial equipment, and consumer electronics, and cheaper or more efficient production can support more output and new fabs. Because disruption remains moderate rather than fully high, the occupation is best classified as resilient, with AI augmenting technicians more than replacing them.

title: Set and exhibit designers
rationale: A large share of set and exhibit design involves digital and cognitive work: interpreting scripts or exhibit goals, generating visual concepts, producing CAD drawings, creating renderings, estimating budgets, and iterating with collaborators. Generative AI, image/video tools, 3D modeling assistants, and automated drafting can materially speed up concept development and documentation, although human judgment, physical feasibility, collaboration, and on-site installation constraints remain central. Demand could expand somewhat because cheaper design enables more small productions, museums, trade shows, retail experiences, and immersive events to afford higher-quality concepts, but total demand is limited by venue capacity, construction costs, production budgets, and the number of shows or exhibits mounted. Because disruption is high but elasticity is only moderate, the occupation is best categorized as restructure: fewer workers may be needed for routine visualization and drafting, while adaptable designers who use AI to deliver richer concepts and manage real-world execution should remain valuable.

title: Sheet metal workers
rationale: Sheet metal work is primarily physical, site-specific, and hands-on: measuring, cutting, bending, fastening, installing, lifting, and working in constrained construction environments. AI may improve peripheral or shop-based tasks such as CADD, takeoffs, estimating, CNC programming, layout optimization, and prefabrication planning, but it is not close to replacing the core installation and fabrication labor at varied worksites. Demand is only modestly elastic because the need for ducts, gutters, siding, and HVAC-related sheet metal is tied to construction, renovation, and building-maintenance cycles rather than unlimited new consumption. Because disruption is low-to-moderate and the core occupation remains grounded in physical skilled trade work, the net effect is resilient.

title: Skincare specialists
rationale: Skincare specialists perform mostly in-person, hands-on services such as facials, waxing, peels, massage, sanitation, and client care, which AI cannot directly substitute without robotics and regulated physical presence. AI can help with skin analysis, product recommendations, appointment scheduling, marketing, and business administration, but these are peripheral or advisory rather than the core service. Demand is moderately elastic because lower-cost, faster, or more personalized skincare could increase treatment frequency and broaden access among price-sensitive clients, though demand is still limited by in-person time, discretionary spending, and personal-service preferences. Because disruption is low and the occupation remains centered on physical, relationship-based care, the net effect is resilient.

title: Small engine mechanics
rationale: Small engine mechanics perform mostly hands-on physical inspection, disassembly, repair, calibration, and reassembly of varied equipment in shops, docks, marinas, and sometimes onsite conditions. AI can help with diagnostic guidance, service manuals, parts identification, customer communication, scheduling, and recordkeeping, but it does not replace the dexterity, tool use, and real-world troubleshooting at the core of the job. Demand would expand only modestly if service became cheaper, because it is tied to the stock of motorcycles, boats, lawn equipment, and generators, though lower costs could shift some customers from replacement to repair. Because disruption is low-to-moderate and the core work remains physical and local, the occupation is best classified as resilient.

title: Social and community service managers
rationale: AI can materially assist with grant writing, reporting to funders, program evaluation, budgeting, scheduling, outreach content, and analysis of service outcomes. However, the core of the occupation involves supervising staff, coordinating with community stakeholders, handling sensitive client and agency issues, and representing programs in local institutional settings, which require trust, judgment, and human presence. Demand for social services is substantial and growing due to aging, mental health, addiction, housing, and poverty-related needs, but expansion is constrained by public funding, nonprofit budgets, regulation, and staffing capacity. Because disruption is meaningful but not enough to automate the core managerial and relational work, the occupation is best classified as resilient.

title: Social and human service assistants
rationale: AI can substantially assist the paperwork-heavy and information-heavy parts of this job, including eligibility screening, benefits navigation, resource research, case notes, scheduling, translation, and follow-up reminders. However, the core work still depends heavily on trust-building, judgment in sensitive situations, coordination with local providers, crisis response, and sometimes in-person visits to homes, shelters, clinics, or community agencies. Demand elasticity is moderate because there is significant unmet need for social services, especially among older adults, people with addictions, homeless clients, and immigrants, but demand is constrained by public funding, housing and treatment capacity, regulations, and the availability of actual services. The occupation is therefore resilient: AI will change workflows and raise caseload capacity, but it is unlikely to replace the human-centered core of the role over the next decade.

title: Social workers
rationale: Social work has substantial cognitive and language-based components—assessment, documentation, treatment planning, benefits navigation, referrals, and psychotherapy—that AI can materially assist through note drafting, triage, resource matching, and client follow-up. However, the core of the occupation still depends on human trust, empathy, licensed judgment, crisis intervention, mandated reporting, advocacy, and often in-person coordination with families, schools, hospitals, courts, and agencies. Demand elasticity is relatively high because mental health care, substance abuse treatment, elder care, child welfare support, and case management all face large unmet need, though public budgets, licensing rules, and reimbursement constraints limit unlimited expansion. Because disruption is meaningful but not high enough to displace the human-centered core, the occupation is best classified as resilient.

title: Sociologists
rationale: Sociology is predominantly cognitive, language- and data-intensive work: literature review, research design, survey and interview analysis, statistical modeling, report writing, and policy recommendations are all areas where AI tools can materially accelerate workflows. However, core tasks still require human judgment about theory, causality, ethics, field context, stakeholder trust, and interpretation of complex social phenomena. Demand could expand somewhat because cheaper research and evaluation would let more governments, nonprofits, universities, and organizations study social problems, but budgets, grant cycles, academic hiring, and policy institutions limit how much demand can grow. The occupation therefore faces substantial task restructuring rather than simple resilience or wholesale replacement.

title: Software developers, quality assurance analysts, and testers
rationale: Software development and QA are almost entirely digital, cognitive tasks, and AI tools already assist materially with coding, debugging, test generation, documentation, code review, and requirements translation. The disruption is not maximum because complex architecture, security, production reliability, stakeholder negotiation, and accountability still require substantial human judgment. Demand elasticity is high because cheaper software development unlocks many more projects across firms, products, automation, cybersecurity, AI, IoT, and internal tooling that were previously too expensive or slow to build. This fits augment: the skill mix will shift sharply toward specification, system design, integration, review, and AI supervision, but expanded demand for software should absorb much of the productivity gain.

title: Solar photovoltaic installers
rationale: Solar PV installation is primarily hands-on, outdoor construction work involving measuring, lifting, mounting, wiring, sealing, testing, and working safely on roofs or job sites. AI can improve system design, site assessment, permitting, scheduling, troubleshooting, and customer proposals, but it does not substantially replace the physical installation work over the next decade. Demand is fairly elastic because lower installation costs would make solar viable for more households, businesses, and utility projects, though adoption is still constrained by roofs, grid interconnection, financing, and policy. Because disruption to the core job is low-to-moderate, the occupation is best classified as resilient despite strong demand growth potential.

title: Special education teachers
rationale: AI can substantially assist special education teachers with lesson adaptation, IEP drafting, progress documentation, assessment analysis, communication with parents, and assistive technologies for students. However, the core work still depends heavily on in-person instruction, behavioral support, emotional regulation, physical assistance, relationship-building, and legally accountable professional judgment. Demand has moderate elasticity because cheaper individualized supports could improve services and expand interventions, but headcount is constrained by school funding, enrollment levels, legal staffing models, and the need for adult supervision. Because disruption is meaningful but not high enough to displace the human-centered core of the occupation, the net effect is resilient.

title: Special effects artists and animators
rationale: This occupation is highly exposed because much of the core work is digital creation, editing, rendering, visual design, and iteration—areas where generative image, video, motion, and 3D tools are already materially changing workflows. Human artistic judgment, story coherence, client direction, and production-pipeline integration remain important, but many routine animation, effects, background, and concepting tasks are directly in AI’s path. Demand has moderate elasticity: cheaper animation and VFX will unlock more indie games, ads, social media content, educational media, and lower-budget productions, but audience attention, studio budgets, IP constraints, and quality-control needs limit unlimited expansion. The occupation therefore is likely to be restructured rather than simply replaced or broadly augmented, with fewer purely production-oriented roles and more emphasis on art direction, prompt/tool fluency, pipeline supervision, and creative integration.

title: Speech-language pathologists
rationale: AI can meaningfully assist speech-language pathologists with documentation, automated speech/language assessment, therapy exercise generation, progress tracking, telepractice, and augmentative communication tools. However, the core work still depends heavily on licensed clinical judgment, rapport with children and medically vulnerable patients, observing nuanced communication behavior, coordinating with families and care teams, and in swallowing cases hands-on clinical evaluation. Demand is fairly elastic because many schools, families, older adults, stroke patients, and underserved communities face unmet needs due to cost, access, and provider shortages, so cheaper AI-enabled services would likely expand screening and treatment intensity. Because disruption is substantial but still bounded by in-person clinical, interpersonal, and regulatory requirements, the occupation is best classified as resilient.

title: Stationary engineers and boiler operators
rationale: AI and advanced controls can improve monitoring, anomaly detection, energy optimization, logging, and predictive maintenance for boilers and building systems. However, the core job still requires licensed human oversight, physical inspection, manual adjustment, troubleshooting, repair, and safety response in hazardous real-world facilities. Demand is fairly inelastic because the number of hospitals, schools, hotels, plants, and large buildings needing steam or mechanical systems is not likely to expand much just because operation becomes cheaper. Because disruption remains low-to-moderate and much of the work requires on-site mechanical presence, the occupation is best categorized as resilient.

title: Substance abuse, behavioral disorder, and mental health counselors
rationale: Counseling is heavily language-based and cognitive: assessment, psychoeducation, treatment planning, progress documentation, and between-session support are all areas where AI tools can materially assist or partially automate. However, the core therapeutic relationship, crisis intervention, mandated-care accountability, clinical judgment, and work with distressed or high-risk clients still require licensed human professionals, keeping disruption from being even higher. Demand elasticity is high because mental health and addiction treatment have large unmet need due to cost, access, stigma, and provider shortages; cheaper AI-enabled care would likely lead to more screening, coaching, follow-up, and lower-acuity support. Because disruption is high but latent demand is also high, AI is more likely to expand counselors’ reach and reshape workflows than simply reduce headcount.

title: Surgical assistants and technologists
rationale: The core work of surgical assistants and technologists is hands-on, sterile, real-time operating-room support: preparing rooms, handling instruments, positioning patients, maintaining sterility, suctioning, suturing, and responding physically during procedures. AI may improve peripheral tasks such as inventory tracking, instrument counting, scheduling, documentation, robotic-equipment setup, and surgical checklists, but it is unlikely to replace the need for trained human presence in the OR over the next decade. Demand elasticity is limited because the number of surgeries is constrained by patient need, surgeons, facilities, insurance coverage, and safety regulation, though cheaper support could modestly expand outpatient capacity. Because disruption is low-to-moderate and the core occupation remains embodied and safety-critical, the net effect is resilient.

title: Survey researchers
rationale: Survey researchers do predominantly cognitive, digital, and language/statistics-based work: drafting questionnaires, choosing methods, cleaning and analyzing data, visualizing results, and writing summaries. AI tools can already materially accelerate survey design, question testing, statistical coding, nonresponse analysis, dashboarding, and report generation, though human judgment remains important for sampling validity, interpretation, ethics, and client needs. Demand has some latent upside because cheaper surveys and analysis could let more organizations run frequent research, but it is constrained by respondent fatigue, sampling quality, privacy limits, and substitution from passive data, social media, and big-data methods. Because disruption is high and elasticity is limited, productivity gains are likely to reduce the need for specialized survey researcher headcount rather than fully expand demand.

title: Surveying and mapping technicians
rationale: AI will materially affect the office and data-processing side of this occupation, including GIS database maintenance, image interpretation, CAD/GIS map updating, error checking, and integration of drone, satellite, and survey data. However, a substantial share of the job still requires real-world field presence: visiting sites, finding or setting markers, operating instruments, dealing with terrain and weather, and verifying conditions on the ground. Demand elasticity is moderate because cheaper mapping and surveying data will support more infrastructure planning, utilities management, environmental monitoring, construction, and digital-twin applications, but many land-survey tasks are tied to fixed construction, property, and regulatory needs. Because disruption is significant but remains capped by physical fieldwork and verification requirements, the occupation fits the resilient category rather than full restructuring or replacement.

title: Surveyors
rationale: Surveying has substantial digital and cognitive components—record searches, GIS/CAD mapping, data validation, report preparation, and legal documentation—that AI, drones, lidar, computer vision, and automated instruments can materially improve. However, the occupation still depends on field presence, site judgment, legal certification, client interaction, and reconciling physical conditions with official records, which limits full automation. Demand is only moderately elastic because surveying is tied to construction, real estate transactions, infrastructure, mining, and legal boundary needs; cheaper surveys may increase usage somewhat, but people will not need dramatically more boundary certifications absent more projects. Because disruption is meaningful but not high enough to replace the core licensed, field-based role, the occupation is best categorized as resilient.

title: Tax examiners and collectors, and revenue agents
rationale: The work is heavily digital, document-based, and rules-driven: reviewing returns, checking deductions and credits against tax law, analyzing financial records, drafting notices, maintaining case files, and prioritizing questionable returns are all in AI’s direct path. Human judgment, legal authority, taxpayer negotiation, and some field audits remain important, especially for complex businesses and collections, but much of the routine examination and correspondence workflow can be automated or AI-assisted. Demand has some latent upside because governments could audit more returns and pursue more delinquent accounts if enforcement became cheaper, but it is capped by budgets, political constraints, due-process requirements, and the finite number of tax filings. Because disruption is high and demand expansion is limited, AI is likely to reduce headcount for routine examiner and collector roles while preserving fewer, more complex human enforcement positions.

title: Taxi drivers, shuttle drivers, and chauffeurs
rationale: Although the job is physically situated in the real world, the core task of operating a vehicle is directly targeted by autonomous-driving AI, and dispatch, routing, pricing, and fleet management are already heavily algorithmic. Full automation will likely be uneven over the next decade because of regulation, weather, liability, passenger assistance, luggage, wheelchair needs, and complex urban edge cases, but robotaxis and autonomous shuttles can materially change the occupation in some markets. Demand would expand if rides became much cheaper, especially for ride-hailing, airport shuttles, older adults, and people without cars, but travel time, trip-purpose limits, and regulation prevent unlimited growth. The result is best classified as restructure: many traditional driving tasks are at risk, while remaining work shifts toward customer assistance, specialized transport, supervision, and operation in geographies or use cases not yet automated.

title: Teacher assistants
rationale: Teacher assistants have a mix of instructional, administrative, supervisory, and caregiving tasks, and AI can materially help with lesson reinforcement, practice exercises, translation, progress tracking, and recordkeeping. However, much of the job depends on in-person classroom presence, behavior management, student supervision, relationship-building, and in special education or childcare settings, hands-on physical assistance that AI cannot replace well over the next decade. Demand for individualized student support is substantial, but public school budgets, staffing models, enrollment levels, and safety requirements limit how much cheaper AI-enabled assistance translates into more teacher-assistant jobs. Because disruption is moderate rather than high, the occupation is best classified as resilient: AI will change tools and workflows, but not fully reshape or absorb the core role.

title: Technical writers
rationale: Technical writing is predominantly digital, language-based knowledge work, and current AI systems can already draft, revise, summarize, translate, standardize, and adapt documentation from specifications, code, tickets, and product notes. Human workers will still be important for validating technical accuracy, interviewing subject-matter experts, understanding user needs, managing documentation architecture, and handling liability-sensitive or highly specialized material. Demand could expand somewhat as cheaper documentation enables better internal knowledge bases, localization, personalized help, and more frequent updates, but it remains constrained by the number of products, regulatory requirements, and organizational willingness to maintain documentation. Because disruption is high but demand expansion is only moderate, the occupation is likely to restructure rather than disappear, with fewer purely drafting roles and more emphasis on technical judgment, information design, and AI-assisted documentation workflows.

title: Telecommunications technicians
rationale: Telecommunications technicians do use digital diagnostics, network monitoring systems, records, and customer communication, so AI can improve troubleshooting, documentation, scheduling, predictive maintenance, and remote guidance. However, the core work is still hands-on installation, repair, cable splicing, equipment setup, climbing, lifting, and working in homes, businesses, central offices, poles, trenches, or towers, which limits direct AI substitution over the next decade. Demand elasticity is fairly low because the need for telecom installation and repair is driven by infrastructure cycles, subscriber locations, permitting, and maintenance requirements rather than simply the cost of technician labor, though cheaper work could modestly accelerate upgrades or small deployments. Because disruption is low-to-moderate and the physical field component remains central, the occupation is best classified as resilient.

title: Tellers
rationale: Teller work is heavily composed of routine transaction processing, identity verification, balance checks, account questions, and electronic recordkeeping, all of which are directly exposed to ATMs, mobile banking, chatbots, remote video tellers, and AI-assisted customer service. Some physical cash handling and in-branch interpersonal service remain, but the core workflow is already being automated and centralized. Demand is highly inelastic because cheaper teller transactions do not cause customers to deposit checks, withdraw cash, or visit branches many times more often; in fact, branch traffic is structurally declining. With high disruption and very low demand expansion, AI and related automation are likely to reduce headcount substantially.

title: Top executives
rationale: Top executives perform highly cognitive work—strategy, budgeting, performance analysis, communications, and policy setting—so AI will materially improve decision support, reporting, scenario analysis, and drafting. However, the core of the role also depends on authority, accountability, leadership, negotiation, organizational legitimacy, and managing people in real institutional contexts, which limits full automation. Demand elasticity is low-to-moderate because the number of executive and general management roles is tied to the number and structure of organizations, not simply the cost of producing analysis or decisions. Because disruption is meaningful but not high enough to replace the human leadership and accountability function, the occupation is best classified as resilient.

title: Tour and travel guides
rationale: AI can materially assist with research, itinerary planning, translation, ticketing, marketing, and even provide automated audio or AR-based narration, so a significant information-delivery portion of the job is exposed. However, the core work still involves in-person presence, group management, hospitality, adapting to weather and crowd conditions, safety, and creating a live social experience, which limits full automation. Demand could expand moderately because cheaper personalized tour content may encourage more visitors to use guided experiences, but travel time, site capacity, and the value of human interaction constrain that expansion. Because disruption is meaningful but not high enough to reshape the occupation’s core physical and interpersonal role, the net effect is resilient.

title: Training and development managers
rationale: Training and development managers do substantial cognitive and digital work: assessing skill gaps, selecting or creating curricula, evaluating program effectiveness, managing learning platforms, and communicating training strategy. AI can materially automate or accelerate needs analysis, content generation, course personalization, vendor comparison, assessment design, and learning analytics, though stakeholder management, organizational judgment, budgeting, and leadership remain human-centered. Demand elasticity is moderate because cheaper customized training will unlock more reskilling, compliance, and employee-development activity, especially as AI changes other jobs, but the number of management roles is still constrained by organizational size and reporting structures. The occupation is therefore likely to be restructured rather than replaced, with managers shifting toward AI-enabled learning strategy, governance, and change management.

title: Training and development specialists
rationale: Training and development specialists perform many language- and knowledge-based tasks that AI can materially accelerate, including drafting learning modules, quizzes, manuals, simulations, surveys, and evaluation reports. However, the occupation also depends on stakeholder consultation, organizational diagnosis, live facilitation, coaching, and change management, which limits full automation. Demand elasticity is high because cheaper training unlocks more frequent upskilling, personalized learning, compliance refreshers, and AI-related workforce retraining that many employers currently underprovide due to cost and time. Because disruption is high but expanded demand for training is likely to absorb much of the productivity gain, the net effect is best characterized as augment.

title: Transportation, storage, and distribution managers
rationale: AI will materially change the planning, routing, inventory monitoring, compliance review, procurement analysis, budgeting, and disruption-response parts of transportation, storage, and distribution management. However, the job still requires human leadership, accountability, on-site operational judgment, safety oversight, labor management, and coordination in physical facilities and transportation networks. Demand can expand as cheaper logistics management supports more e-commerce, faster delivery expectations, and more complex supply chains, but it is still constrained by physical goods volumes, facilities, fleets, and labor. Because disruption is high while demand elasticity is moderate, the occupation is best categorized as restructure: fewer managers may oversee more operations using AI, and the skill mix will shift toward systems supervision, exception handling, and cross-functional coordination.

title: Travel agents
rationale: Travel agents perform highly digital, language- and information-processing tasks: eliciting preferences, comparing fares and schedules, building itineraries, explaining rules, and making reservations. Generative AI and travel platforms can already automate much of trip research, itinerary construction, customer Q&A, and rebooking support, although humans retain value for complex, luxury, group, and emergency travel situations. Demand elasticity is limited because the main constraint on travel is travelers’ time and trip budgets, not the cost of planning itself, though cheaper personalized planning may expand use somewhat. Because disruption is high and elasticity is low, AI is likely to reduce headcount among generalist agents while preserving more specialized advisory roles.

title: Tutors
rationale: Tutoring is highly exposed because many core tasks—explaining concepts, generating practice questions, giving feedback, adapting pacing, tracking progress, and preparing for tests—are language- and knowledge-based tasks that AI systems can already perform meaningfully. Human tutors still add value through motivation, trust, behavioral management, special-needs support, and relationships with parents or teachers, so the occupation is not fully automatable. Demand elasticity is very high because individualized academic help has historically been constrained by cost, scheduling, and access, and cheaper AI-enabled tutoring could greatly expand how many students receive support and how often. The net effect is augment: routine tutoring tasks will be heavily automated, but expanded access and AI-assisted human coaching should absorb much of the productivity gain while substantially changing how tutors work.

title: Umpires, referees, and other sports officials
rationale: AI and computer vision can meaningfully assist with specific officiating tasks such as line calls, strike zones, timing, replay review, and detection of some rule violations, especially in professional and televised sports. However, the core job still requires real-time physical presence, positioning, judgment under ambiguous conditions, player safety oversight, communication, and dispute management in unpredictable live environments, particularly at youth, school, and recreational levels where most events lack advanced infrastructure. Demand for officiating is mostly tied to the number of games, teams, facilities, and sports participation, so making calls cheaper or faster would not create dramatically more sporting events. Because disruption is moderate rather than high, the occupation is best classified as resilient despite some task-level automation.

title: Urban and regional planners
rationale: Urban and regional planners do substantial digital and cognitive work—GIS analysis, demographic and environmental data synthesis, zoning research, report writing, scenario modeling, and presentation preparation—that AI can materially accelerate. However, the core occupation also depends heavily on stakeholder meetings, public process, local political judgment, site-specific context, regulatory accountability, and recommendations that must be defended to officials and communities. Demand could expand moderately if planning analysis becomes cheaper, especially for smaller jurisdictions and more frequent scenario testing, but public budgets, permitting timelines, and statutory processes limit how much additional planning work is consumed. Because AI reshapes many analytical tasks but does not replace the human-facing and governance-centered core, the occupation is best classified as resilient.

title: Veterinarians
rationale: Veterinary work is a mixed occupation: AI can assist with diagnostic decision support, imaging interpretation, lab result review, records, client communication, and triage, but much of the core work involves hands-on exams, animal handling, surgery, wound care, vaccination, euthanasia, and emotionally sensitive owner interactions. Licensing, liability, and the need to work with unpredictable animals in clinics, farms, and other real-world settings limit full automation over the next decade. Demand has moderate elasticity because high costs currently suppress some pet care, diagnostics, preventive services, and advanced treatments, but total demand is constrained by pet populations, owner budgets, and the physical nature of care delivery. Because disruption is moderate rather than high, AI is more likely to augment veterinarians and clinic workflows than reshape or replace the occupation.

title: Veterinary assistants and laboratory animal caretakers
rationale: The core work is hands-on animal care: feeding, cleaning cages, restraining animals, moving patients, assisting during procedures, administering medications, and monitoring recovery in unpredictable physical environments. AI can help with peripheral tasks such as scheduling, recordkeeping, inventory, owner communication, remote monitoring, and possibly some lab-animal facility automation, but it does not substitute for safe animal handling and in-person support. Demand has moderate elasticity because lower-cost support could enable more routine veterinary care, boarding, procedures, and research capacity, but growth is constrained by pet ownership, veterinarians, facilities, regulation, and the inherently physical nature of care. Because disruption is low-to-moderate and AI mainly augments the periphery rather than reshaping the occupation, the net effect is resilient.

title: Veterinary technologists and technicians
rationale: AI can assist veterinary technologists and technicians with recordkeeping, client communication, lab interpretation, imaging support, inventory, scheduling, and monitoring alerts, but much of the job involves hands-on animal handling, restraint, medication administration, anesthesia monitoring, specimen collection, and direct clinical support in unpredictable physical settings. The demand elasticity is moderate because cheaper and faster veterinary support could enable more preventive care, diagnostics, chronic disease management, and treatment options for pets, but demand is still constrained by pet populations, household budgets, clinic capacity, and veterinarian supervision. Because the core work remains substantially physical, clinical, and in-person, AI is more likely to augment peripheral and diagnostic workflows than reshape or replace the occupation. Therefore the net effect is resilient.

title: Waiters and waitresses
rationale: Waiters and waitresses perform some routine cognitive and transactional tasks—taking orders, entering them in POS systems, answering menu questions, and processing payments—that are already being affected by kiosks, QR-code ordering, mobile payment, and AI-enabled customer interfaces. However, much of the core job still requires physical presence, carrying food and drinks, clearing tables, handling exceptions, reading social cues, and providing hospitality in a variable real-world environment. Demand for table service would expand only modestly if these tasks became cheaper, because restaurant demand is constrained by food costs, seating capacity, location, consumer time, and the social nature of dining. The occupation is therefore resilient: AI and self-service technology will reduce some labor per table and change workflows, but they are unlikely to fully reshape or absorb the core work over the next decade.

title: Water and wastewater treatment plant and system operators
rationale: AI and advanced automation can materially improve process monitoring, chemical dosing, anomaly detection, predictive maintenance, and regulatory reporting, especially through SCADA-like systems and sensor analytics. However, the occupation still requires licensed human oversight, on-site inspection, sampling, equipment cleaning and maintenance, safety procedures, and emergency response in unpredictable physical environments. Demand elasticity is very low because communities do not need dramatically more drinking-water or wastewater treatment simply because operator labor becomes cheaper; demand is tied mainly to population, infrastructure, and regulation. The net effect is resilient because AI will reduce some staffing needs and change workflows, but the core job remains a mixed physical-operational role rather than fully automatable digital work.

title: Water transportation workers
rationale: AI can assist with navigation, route optimization, collision avoidance, engine monitoring, predictive maintenance, recordkeeping, and dispatch coordination, but much of the work still requires physical presence aboard vessels, hands-on maintenance, safety response, passenger interaction, and regulatory accountability. Autonomous and remotely operated vessels may reduce some watchstanding and routine piloting tasks over time, but adoption is constrained by safety, liability, port operations, weather, legacy fleets, and Coast Guard and international maritime regulation. Demand is relatively inelastic because employment is tied mainly to cargo volumes, commodity flows, ferry needs, tourism, and port activity rather than the price of mariner labor alone. Because disruption is moderate rather than high, AI is likely to augment and streamline operations without reshaping the occupation’s core enough to move it out of the resilient category.

title: Web developers and digital designers
rationale: Web development and digital design are almost entirely digital tasks involving code generation, interface design, prototyping, testing, content integration, and analytics, all of which are directly affected by current AI tools. AI can already produce layouts, write and debug front-end code, generate mockups, and automate parts of QA, though humans remain important for client requirements, product judgment, accessibility, brand fit, and complex integration. Demand elasticity is high because cheaper web and interface production enables more businesses, campaigns, products, personalization, A/B testing, and mobile or ecommerce experiences, although simple brochure sites will be heavily automated. Because disruption is very high but cheaper output is likely to unlock substantial additional digital work, the occupation is best classified as augment, with major restructuring of skills toward AI-assisted design, product thinking, and integration.

title: Welders, cutters, solderers, and brazers
rationale: Welding, cutting, soldering, and brazing are primarily hands-on physical tasks requiring manual dexterity, spatial judgment, safety awareness, and work in varied real-world environments, which limits direct AI substitution. AI-enabled robotics and machine vision can automate repetitive welds in structured manufacturing settings and help with inspection, quality control, and blueprint interpretation, but much field, repair, custom, and confined-space work remains difficult to automate. Demand could expand somewhat if fabrication became cheaper, but it is largely derived from construction, infrastructure, repair, and manufacturing activity, which are constrained by materials, capital budgets, regulation, and broader economic cycles. Because disruption is low-to-moderate rather than high, the occupation is best classified as resilient despite some automation pressure in factories.

title: Wholesale and manufacturing sales representatives
rationale: AI can materially automate or accelerate many core sales-rep tasks: prospect identification, lead scoring, personalized outreach, product explanations, quote generation, CRM updates, follow-ups, and routine order processing. Human reps remain important for complex B2B relationships, technical demonstrations, negotiation, trade shows, and trust-building, but inside sales and lower-complexity product categories are directly exposed to chatbots, self-service portals, and AI sales assistants. Demand elasticity is limited because the underlying demand for wholesale and manufactured goods is not created mainly by the cost of sales labor, and buyers have finite attention for outreach, though AI may expand coverage of small accounts. With high disruption and relatively low demand expansion, productivity gains are likely to reduce the need for many routine sales roles while preserving fewer, more consultative account-management positions.

title: Wind turbine technicians
rationale: Wind turbine technicians perform heavily physical, safety-critical work at height, including climbing towers, inspecting equipment, replacing components, and repairing mechanical, electrical, and hydraulic systems. AI can improve remote monitoring, predictive maintenance, fault diagnosis, documentation, scheduling, and drone-based visual inspection, but it does not replace the core hands-on repair and field presence required. Demand is moderately elastic because cheaper maintenance can lower wind power operating costs and support more turbine deployment, but the number of jobs is still constrained by installed turbine capacity, permitting, grid buildout, and physical maintenance needs. Because disruption remains low-to-moderate despite useful AI tools, the occupation is best categorized as resilient.

title: Woodworkers
rationale: Woodworking includes some digital and technical tasks, such as reading drawings, programming or setting up CNC machines, optimizing cuts, and checking specifications, where AI-enabled design, toolpath generation, vision inspection, and maintenance systems can help. However, the core work still involves physical materials, machine tending, lifting, assembly, finishing, safety judgment, and hands-on adjustment to wood variability, so AI changes the periphery more than the center of the occupation. Demand could expand somewhat for cheaper customized cabinets, furniture, renovation products, and small-batch wood goods, but it is constrained by housing activity, durable-goods replacement cycles, material costs, and physical production capacity. Because disruption is moderate rather than high, the occupation is best classified as resilient, even though automation will continue to reduce some routine machine-operator roles.

title: Writers and authors
rationale: Writing and authorship are almost entirely language-based, digital, and cognitive tasks, and current AI systems can already draft, revise, summarize research, generate ideas, adapt tone, and produce marketing or informational copy at scale. Human writers remain important for original reporting, lived experience, distinctive voice, client relationships, taste, accountability, and high-end creative work, but the workflow and required skills will change substantially. Demand for written content will expand as cheaper production enables more blogs, newsletters, ads, scripts, self-publishing, localization, and personalized content, but audience attention, brand trust, editorial standards, and fixed media budgets limit how much this expansion translates into more writer headcount. The result is restructuring: many routine writing tasks are automated or compressed, while successful writers increasingly act as editors, creative directors, subject-matter experts, prompt users, and curators of AI-assisted output.

title: Zoologists and wildlife biologists
rationale: AI will materially affect the analytical and documentation-heavy parts of this occupation, including GIS modeling, population estimation, literature review, statistical analysis, image/acoustic species identification, and report writing. However, a large share of core work still involves field observation, specimen collection, animal handling, ecological context, remote travel, and coordination with agencies and conservation stakeholders, which limits full automation. Demand could expand somewhat because cheaper monitoring and modeling would make more habitats and species feasible to study, but employment is heavily constrained by government and nonprofit budgets, permitting, and policy priorities. Because disruption is meaningful but not high enough to reshape the entire occupation, the net effect is resilient.
